_comment: Spot Finder tool. AutoForm over SpotFinderViewModel: a Detection dock (file list, workflow selector, the settings that deviate from it, an analysis region, Detect/Preview/Export) plus result docks (the field with the found regions marked, and the run table with one row per input). Writes each detection into its measurement's own container, for the Region MLE panel below to fit.

sections.title: Imaging files
sections.description: Photon or camera image file(s) to detect in. Drag-drop to add.

sections.label: Workflow
sections.description: The recipe. single_molecule is the standard one — the pipeline the Region MLE has always been fitted on. Picking a workflow replaces every setting below with that recipe's; edit them afterwards to deviate from it.

sections.label: Detection name
sections.description: Stem the regions are stored under, so two detections of the same field can be compared instead of one replacing the other.

sections.title: Analysis region
sections.description: Confines the search. The threshold is computed from these pixels alone, so the rest of the frame does not set it — which is the point of restricting an analysis to one cell or one illuminated patch. Empty = the whole frame.

sections.label: Method
sections.description: watershed splits objects that touch; threshold does not, which is right when they do not; log and dog measure each spot's own width.

sections.label: Threshold
sections.description: Intensity level; below 0 computes an Otsu level. For log/dog this is the minimum scale-normalised response instead, which does not follow the image units — read it off a run.

sections.label: Smoothing σ
sections.description: Gaussian smoothing before thresholding. Smoothing is what stops a single noisy pixel becoming an object.

sections.label: Peak footprint
sections.description: Square footprint side for the watershed's local-maxima seeds. Larger merges nearby seeds, which is how over-splitting is cured.

sections.label: min σ
sections.description: Smallest spot width to look for, in pixels. A diffraction-limited spot has σ ≈ 0.21 λ / NA.

sections.label: max σ
sections.description: Largest spot width to look for, in pixels.

sections.label: Scales
sections.description: Number of scales between them (log only).

sections.label: Overlap
sections.description: Spots overlapping by more than this fraction are merged, the larger kept.

sections.label: Min area (px)
sections.description: Smaller regions are dropped. 2 is what separates an object from a hot camera pixel: a spot covers several pixels, a defect covers exactly one.

sections.label: Max area (px)
sections.description: Larger regions are dropped; 0 disables. An aggregate is not a molecule, and it is the one that dominates a brightness histogram.

sections.label: Clear border
sections.description: Drop regions touching the frame edge. A partly-imaged object has a truncated area and a biased centroid — but on a crowded field this can remove most of the data.

sections.label: Fit window (px)
sections.description: Side of the square the fit sees. Wide enough to hold background as well as the spot — a window cropped to the spot has no baseline — and narrow enough not to contain the neighbouring spot, which is what pulls a fit sideways.

buttons.label: ➕ Add picks
buttons.description: Turn the picked spots into regions of this detection, so they are written and fitted like any other.

buttons.label: 👁️ Preview
buttons.description: Detect in the first file only, writing nothing — for tuning against the region count.

buttons.label: ▶ Detect
buttons.description: Detect in every selected file and write each result into its own measurement container.

buttons.label: 💾 Export
buttons.description: Export the combined region table (all files) to a TSV/CSV.

sections.title: Regions
sections.description: Browse what was found; the canvas marks the selected region and the panel shows its measurements. **Click the image to pick a spot the detector missed** — the click seeds a 2-D Gaussian fit, and the fit decides where the spot is and how wide it is.

sections.title: Run

columns.label: File
columns.description: The input, whatever became of it.

columns.label: Written to
columns.description: The measurement container the pair was written into.

columns.label: Reason
columns.description: Why, for anything that is not ok.

sections.description: One row per input file, whatever became of it. A file that produced nothing is a row saying so, never a file that quietly left the list.
